contracts.text: A container type named Validated must exist.
A concrete subtype named Valid must exist, representing success.
A concrete subtype named Invalid must exist, representing accumulated failures.
Invalid must store its errors in an immutable tuple (the type annotation must indicate a tuple).
Invalid.from_failure(error) must wrap the single error into a 1-tuple so that Invalid((error,)) is produced.
contracts.adverse_condition: error is itself a tuple — wrapping must still produce a 1-tuple containing that tuple, not flatten it.

contracts.text: When apply combines two Invalid containers, the resulting error tuple must be self's errors concatenated with the other's errors, preserving stable left-to-right order.
contracts.adverse_condition: Both Invalid containers hold errors that are pairwise distinguishable — identical or commutative error sets cannot reveal order violations.

contracts.text: swap on Valid(x) must return Invalid((x,)).
contracts.adverse_condition: x is itself a tuple; swap must wrap the whole tuple in another 1-tuple, e.g. Valid((1,2)) → Invalid(((1,2),)).

contracts.text: swap on Invalid(errs) must return Valid(errs), where the error tuple becomes the valid value.
from_validated classmethod must return the same instance it receives (identity, not just equality).
alt on Invalid must apply the provided function to each individual error element in the tuple and return a new Invalid with the mapped results.
contracts.adverse_condition: The error tuple contains multiple elements; each must be independently mapped. If elements are identical after mapping, correctness of per-element application may be hidden.

contracts.text: Valid must define __match_args__ to support structural pattern matching.
Invalid must define __match_args__ to support structural pattern matching.
Validated must support equality comparison.
Validated must support repr.
Validated must support do-notation.
Validated must have an unwrap method.
Validated must have a failure method.
Validated must have a value_or method.
Validated must have a from_value classmethod or constructor.
Validated must have a bind_validated method.
bind on Invalid must short-circuit: it must not apply the bound function and must return the Invalid (or an equivalent Invalid with the same errors).
contracts.adverse_condition: The Validated is Invalid. The bound function, if erroneously called, might produce a side-effect or return a different Validated — the contract requires it is never invoked.

contracts.text: from_result classmethod: given a Success(value), it must produce Valid(value).
from_result classmethod: given a Failure(error), it must produce Invalid((error,)) with the error wrapped in a 1-tuple.
contracts.adverse_condition: error is itself a tuple; it must be wrapped in another tuple, not flattened.

contracts.text: A pointfree bind_validated function must be exported from the returns.pointfree package (in __init__.py).
combine classmethod: given two Valid containers and a binary function, it must produce Valid(f(x, y)) using applicative combination.
contracts.adverse_condition: Both inputs are Valid but their values are identical or the function is commutative — this can hide argument-order errors.

contracts.text: combine classmethod: given at least one Invalid, it must accumulate errors from all Invalid inputs into a single Invalid whose error tuple is the concatenation of all individual error tuples.
contracts.adverse_condition: Multiple Invalid inputs carry errors; the concatenation order (self's errors before other's errors) must be preserved.

contracts.text: combine_n classmethod: given a tuple of N Validated containers all being Valid and an N-ary function, it must produce Valid(f(v1, ..., vN)).
contracts.adverse_condition: All inputs are Valid but some values are identical or the function is commutative over swapped arguments — this can hide positional argument errors.

contracts.text: combine_n classmethod: if any of the N Validated containers is Invalid, it must accumulate all errors from every Invalid container into a single Invalid.
contracts.adverse_condition: Multiple containers are Invalid; errors from a later Invalid could be mistakenly omitted while only the first Invalid's errors are kept.

contracts.text: The result_to_validated converter function must exist in the converters module and convert a Result into a Validated.
The validated_to_result converter function must exist in the converters module and convert a Validated into a Result.
The validated decorator must catch exceptions raised by the wrapped function and return Invalid containing the caught exception.
contracts.adverse_condition: The wrapped function raises an exception. If no exception is raised, the decorator must not alter the return value into an Invalid.

contracts.text: The validated decorator must support an exceptions parameter that restricts which exception types are caught (others propagate normally).
contracts.adverse_condition: The wrapped function raises an exception type not listed in exceptions — it must propagate, not be caught.

contracts.text: The validated decorator must preserve the wrapped function's __name__.
The ValidatedLikeN interface must extend FailableN directly (not DiverseFailableN).
ValidatedLikeN must define its own from_failure classmethod.
ValidatedLikeN must define custom short-circuit law specifications for map on failure values.
ValidatedLikeN must define custom short-circuit law specifications for bind on failure values.
ValidatedLikeN must define custom short-circuit law specifications for apply on failure values.
returns/methods/cond.py must include a dispatch branch for ValidatedLikeN, placed before the container_type.empty fallback.
returns/contrib/hypothesis/containers.py must register ValidatedLikeN with from_failure strategy generation.
returns/pointfree/__init__.py must export bind_validated.
All work must be done on a new branch created from main.
All changes must be committed when done.
No changes to returns/iterables.py are permitted; Fold.collect must work automatically through apply with no modifications.
The combine classmethod must correctly map each positional input to its corresponding function-argument position: the first Validated maps to the first parameter, the second to the second parameter.
contracts.adverse_condition: Both Validated values are Valid and pairwise distinguishable, and the binary function is non-commutative.

contracts.text: The combine_n classmethod must correctly map each positional Validated in the tuple to its corresponding N-ary function-argument position.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least two Validated values in the tuple are Valid and pairwise distinguishable, and the N-ary function is non-commutative with respect to those positions.
